articles.title: Traffic curbs in Delhi for INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan on November 1 | LIVE
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP) on Saturday (October 31) questioned the timing of the INDIA bloc’s November 1 rally being held amid Diwali festivities and said that ignoring festivals, social harmony and the country’s economy in the name of politics is not a good sign for political parties.

The RSS affiliate pointed out that Congress leader Rahul Gandhi’s Bharat Jodo Yatra, held between September 2022 and January 2023, had a nine-day break from December 25 to January 2 for Christmas and New Year celebrations.

However, despite repeated appeals by traders’ organisations in Delhi and members of Hindu society to cancel or postpone the November 1 rally, their pleas have fallen on deaf ears, VHP national spokesperson Vinod Bansal said in a post on X.
Traffic restrictions will be in place across parts of Delhi from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. on November 1 in view of an INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan, police said.

Traffic diversions will be enforced at key intersections in central Delhi, including Netaji Subhash Marg T-point, Rajghat, Delhi Gate, ITO A-point, Ajmeri Gate red light, Ranjeet Singh Flyover, Jhandewalan roundabout, Turkman Gate and Mirdard Chowk, depending on the traffic situation, the Delhi Traffic Police said.

Commuters are likely to face congestion on Bahadur Shah Zafar Marg between ITO and Delhi Gate, Jawaharlal Nehru Marg between Rajghat and Ajmeri Gate, Aruna Asaf Ali Road, Minto Road, Desh Bandhu Gupta Road and Barakhamba Road, as well as stretches around Kamla Market and Hamdard Chowk.
Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge has refused to comment on whether CJP leaders will participate in the November 1 rally in Delhi planned by the opposition against SIR .
PTI had on Thursday (October 28) erroneously reported that Mr. Kharge had replied in the negative taking note of his gesture. However, his office clarified he did not wish to comment on the question.

The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has extended support to the November 1 rally. The outfit, founded by Abhijeet Dipke, said it would support organisations fighting for free and fair elections and reiterated its demand for Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation.

Ahead of the INDIA bloc’s November 1 rally at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan against “vote chori”, the Haryana Congress on Friday held meetings in Karnal, Panipat and Sonipat for finalising a strategy to ensure maximum participation at the event from the state, party leaders said.
The Congress in-charge for Haryana, Sanjay Dutt, and State unit president, Rao Narendra Singh, took part in the meetings with senior party leaders, district office-bearers and workers.

The meetings reviewed the preparations for the ‘Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao’ rally in Delhi, which will be led by Congress leader Rahul Gandhi at the Ramlila Maidan as part of the opposition bloc’s campaign against alleged electoral irregularities and the demand for the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

articles.title: KTR questions proposed sale of IDBI Bank, asks if its valuable real estate assets were factored in valuation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) working president K.T. Rama Rao has questioned the Union government’s proposed sale of IDBI Bank to a private player , raising concerns over the bank’s valuation, changes in bidding norms and the treatment of its real estate assets.

In a post on X, KTR said public sector undertakings (PSUs) and public sector banks were national assets that needed to be safeguarded. He said reports about the alleged undervaluation of IDBI Bank were a matter of concern and sought to know why the rules and valuation methodology were changed after bids fell below the reserve price.
He also questioned whether the bank’s valuable real estate assets, including prime land in Hyderabad, were adequately factored into the valuation.
KTR sought to know why the concerns raised by IDBI Bank employees over the proposed disinvestment were not being addressed.

Before selling a reputed public sector bank to a private entity, the Union government owed the country clear answers on the valuation and the process being followed, he said. Questioning the urgency behind the proposed sale, the BRS leader asked: “What’s the hurry?”.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Congress, VCK mobilise cadres for Nov. 1 INDIA bloc protest in New Delhi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, the Tamil Nadu Congress Committee (TNCC) and Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi (VCK) have activated their respective party machineries to mobilise cadres for the INDIA bloc protest to be held on November 1, 2026, in New Delhi.

While the bulk of the heavy lifting would be done by the Indian National Congress, which is much stronger in and around New Delhi, the TNCC leaders, on their part, are expected to mobilise at least 150 people from every district in Tamil Nadu.
Mayiladuthurai MP R. Sudha said that the party’s rank and file are enthusiastic and have heeded the call of Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, who is expected to lead the protest.

“We expect more than five lakh Congress cadres to participate. From Tamil Nadu, we are expecting at least 100 party workers to reach New Delhi from each district. Apart from them, the office-bearers of the Mahila Congress, Youth Congress, and other party wings will also participate,” she said.

While the Congress party is mobilising people from across the country, Ms. Sudha alleged that the BJP-led Centre was trying to curtail the privileges of Members of Parliament by not allowing Emergency Quotas in trains and not providing accommodation to their guests.

“EQ is not being released. Family members are not being given accommodation, which we are usually allotted. Congress MPs, in particular, are being singled out. They are curtailing our privileges and our movement. This is an undeclared emergency,” she said.

A senior VCK leader said that the party has asked its organs in Tamil Nadu and across southern States such as Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, and Keralam to mobilise a modest number of party cadres for the protest in New Delhi.

articles.title: Operation underway to recover bodies from remote chopper crash site in Uttarakhand
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Operations to recover the bodies of the six victims of the helicopter crash in Uttarakhand resumed on Saturday (October 31, 2026) morning, officials said.

Rescue work started at 5 a.m. on Saturday (October 31, 2026) but the recovery from the remote area would be difficult, they said. The operation had been halted on Friday (October 30, 2026) due to darkness, the presence of wild bears and other animals and difficult terrain.

A privately run helicopter carrying pilgrims from Badrinath crashed into a hillside in Joshimath in Uttarakhand, killing all six of its occupants. The helicopter, operated by Trans Bharat Aviation, was returning from the Badrinath shrine to Dehradun.
The bodies of the pilot and the five pilgrims from Karnataka were found in the vicinity of the wreckage in Chai village.
The district administration said that on Saturday (October 31, 2026) morning a team from the forest department was also dispatched to the site to recover the bodies.
A team from the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB), which is probing the crash, will also be reaching the site on the day.
Speaking to reporters, Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami said that orders have been issued to investigate and determine the exact cause of the accident.

"We pray to God to grant the departed souls a place at his divine feet and give strength to their families and loved ones, who are going through immense grief and trauma during this difficult time," Mr. Dhami said.

Prateek Jain, CEO, Uttarakhand Civil Aviation Development Authority (UCADA) told PTI , "The bodies were found but the recovery is difficult due to the terrain. The mortal remains will be brought to Chamoli district headquarters via a trek and after post-mortem examination, it will be brought to Dehradun."
When asked about permission for flying despite an alert issued by IMD, Mr. Jain said, "We had also issued an advisory but that is in the scope of investigation now."
On Friday (October 30, 2026), officials had informed that after recovery, the bodies will be brought to Joshimath town where post-mortem will be conducted on Saturday (October 31, 2026).
The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has also said that its team has been dispatched to Dehradun to conduct a preliminary and regulatory assessment of the accident.

articles.title: ABVP holds ‘Save Democracy’ march in Patna amid SIR row
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) members on Friday (October 30, 2026) took out a protest march in Bihar’s Patna under the campaign ‘ Loktantra Bachao Arajakta Hatao’ (Save Democracy, End Anarchy).

Hitting out at the Congress party, the ABVP members gathered at Kargil Chowk to convey the message of unity against alleged attempts to weaken democracy and democratic institutions. Despite continuous rainfall, a large number of students and activists from various districts of north Bihar and south Bihar participated in the programme.

Holding the national flag and ABVP flag, the protesters crossed the police barricades and marched towards Dak Bungalow Chauraha, where the rally concluded. ABVP National Secretary Abhay Pratap Singh and newly elected Delhi University Students’ Union (DUSU) President Yash Dabas were leading the march.
The protesters also broke the police barricading near JP Golambar before reaching Dak Bungalow and attempted to stand on the barricading.

Addressing the gathering, Mr. Singh said, “India is a democratic country where governments are formed and changed through the people’s votes, not through demonstrations of strength on the streets. Anarchy aimed at changing governments in India, inspired by political developments in Bangladesh and Nepal, is unacceptable.”

“Amid questions surrounding the role of external forces, it is clear that India’s political direction will be determined by Indian citizens. The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls is a regular administrative process, and allegations of irregularities in it should be raised before constitutional forums with supporting evidence,” he added.

Mr. Singh pointed out that raising questions about the credibility of institutions like the Election Commission of India (ECI) and the Supreme Court for political interests, and attempting to bring them under pressure, goes against democratic principles.

“Those who are dreaming to bring a change of Government in India through anarchy, must understand that India’s democracy is strong and the future of Governments here is decided by the people,”Mr. Singh said.

ABVP called upon the youth of the country to remain vigilant in protecting the dignity of constitutional institutions, democratic values and national interest, and to oppose the politics of anarchy and mobocracy through democratic means.

“The roots of India’s youth lie in its rich cultural heritage, civilisational consciousness and sense of duty towards the nation. India’s youth take pride in their cultural identity and believe in positive, constructive and democratic approaches to resolve the country’s challenges,’ Mr. Dabas said.

He also said that through the student march in Patna, students have made it clear that the energy of Indian youth will be channelled towards nation-building, social harmony and strengthening the country’s cultural heritage.

articles.title: Two militants held for 'involvement' in kidnapping of woman in Manipur
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Two members of a proscribed outfit were arrested for allegedly being involved in the kidnapping of a woman in Manipur's Imphal East district, police said on Saturday (October 31, 2026).

A joint team of police commandos and 31st Assam Rifles personnel apprehended the two militants, who belong to the banned Kangleipak Communist Party (Nongdrenkhomba), on Thursday (October 29), a police statement said.
"They have been suspected of being involved in the kidnapping of a woman from Top Awang Leikai in Imphal East district on September 3," police said.
A firearm along with ammunition and a car were seized from their possession, it said.
Security forces have been conducting search operations in Manipur since ethnic violence broke out in the State three years ago.

The ethnic conflict that erupted in May 2023 between the valley-based Meitei and hill-based Kuki communities has claimed at least 306 lives, while 49 people remain missing and thousands have been left homeless. In recent months, clashes between Kuki and Naga communities have also been reported.

articles.title: Disinvestment as key economic strategy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: S even months into 2026-27, the fiscal year has been shaped by global uncertainty, high energy prices and worries over a deficient monsoon. Against this backdrop, disinvestment and asset monetisation have helped in navigating a challenging fiscal year. While receipts were already on course to meet the budget target, the government’s approval of the sale of its share in the IDBI Bank on October 14 makes it likely that the target will be exceeded. For the industry and investors, the receipts are a signal of the government’s continued commitment to reforms and a larger role for the private sector. This year so far, the disinvestment trajectory has progressed well, even before the IDBI stake sale. According to DIPAM data, the Centre mobilised ₹62,124 crore in April-September 2026 through disinvestment and asset monetisation, of which ₹55,757 crore came from disinvestment. These collections had already reached 78% of the full-year budget target of ₹80,000 crore. With the IDBI proceeds, the collections are to head past the target.

This comes at a time when the government looks to diversify its revenue sources amid rising expenditure commitments. Net tax revenue rose by a modest 3.4% in April-August 2026 and non-tax revenue by 3.2%, while capital expenditure was up by over 18%. Overall, the fiscal deficit has already reached 42% of the budgeted levels which implies a tight balance between revenue shortfalls and spending risks.

articles.title: Coal India profit jumps 57% as higher offtake, prices weigh over costs
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Coal India’s net profit surged 57% year-on-year (YoY) to ₹6,547 crore in the second quarter, driven by higher offtake and improved price realisations that offset an increase in input costs.
The state-owned coal miner declared a second interim dividend of ₹10.25 per equity share.

Offtake during the quarter ended September increased 12% YoY to 186.34 million tonnes (MT), primarily driven by higher power demand. Average price realisation, covering fuel supply agreements, e-auctions, washed coal and other categories, rose 7% YoY to ₹2,346.21 per tonne.
The Kolkata-headquartered company’s overall production grew 4% YoY to 151.37 MT in the reported quarter, falling short of its target of 157.83 MT.
Revenue from the sale of products increased 21% YoY to ₹43,724 crore. Overall revenue also rose 21% to ₹44,179 crore.

The company’s cost of materials -- which primarily includes expenditure on explosives, oil and lubricants, heavy earth-moving machinery, spares and timber, among other items -- increased 20% YoY to ₹2,752 crore during the quarter.

articles.title: Deepavali sales expected to gain momentum in Coimbatore next week
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Shopping for the Deepavali festival in Coimbatore city this year is expected to pick up next week across sectors.
President of the Indian Chamber of Commerce and Industry, Coimbatore, C. Dorairaj, told The Hindu on Thursday (October 29) that several companies in Coimbatore will disburse bonuses next week.

With the festival coming in the first week of a month this year, people are likely to start purchases after getting the monthly salary and the festival bonus. So, the last 5-6 days preceding the festival is expected to see huge retail activity.
Be it textiles, FMCG, or household appliances, the retailers are expecting good sales this year.

All the products have seen a price hike, ranging between 10% and 30%, in the last few months, depending on the product. So, the retailers may see higher revenue though the volume of sales may remain the same as last year or slightly better in some sectors, he added.

In the case of textiles, while the large, multi brand retail outlets are already witnessing a pick up of sales, the smaller outlets are facing stiff competition from online sellers. Further, business at the small retail shops will go up in the last few days before the festival.

The household appliances outlets are also expecting better sales only from next week.
In the case of sweets and savouries, most of the bulk buyers will purchase products for distribution just days before the festival, Mr. Dorairaj said.

articles.title: U.S. Fed holds rates steady; pressure on emerging markets expected with stronger dollar outlook
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The U.S. Federal Reserve held its benchmark interest rates unchanged between 3.75% and 4.0% at its October policy meeting. The 12-member committee had a 10:2 voting pattern for maintaining the status quo, while Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Federal President Beth Hammack voted in favour of a 25 basis points hike.
The Fed decision comes against the backdrop of sticky inflation, with the central bank awaiting more incoming economic data before changing the Fed Funds target range.

The Fed’s policy decision was broadly in line with market expectations, with Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh announcing the Fed would reduce the number of Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings beginning 2027.

One of the FOMC meetings from next year onwards will exclusively address broader monetary policy strategy than rate-setting. In 2028, the Fed is expected to hold two meetings focused on monetary policy strategy, with the rest six meetings for policy, Mr. Warsh said.
While the policy decision was factored in by market participants, the absence of forward guidance by Mr. Warsh makes gauging the longevity of higher interest rate regime uncertain.
“I don’t believe in forward guidance, absent exigent circumstances, absent a crisis,” Mr. Warsh said. The market currently prices another rate hike by a quarter percentage point in December.

The U.S. Fed is expected to keep rates elevated, making U.S. Treasuries and the dollar relatively more attractive than emerging market (EM) economies for foreign investors. Combined with the escalating West Asia crisis, EM economies are expected to witness volatility and foreign fund outflow, economists noted.
On Thursday (October 29, 2026), the Indian market did not dramatically react to the Fed’s rate decision as it was mostly expected.

However, the Indian rupee declined to its lowest level in nearly 2 weeks on Thursday (October 29, 2026) following continued dollar demand. The rupee traded between 95.30-95.36 a dollar, down 8-14 paise from its previous close. While most other Asian currencies traded higher following the rate-decision, the Indian rupee continued to weaken.

However, economists are of the view that rupee is currently priced based on fundamental concerns and not on interest rates. This means the rupee’s depreciation is a direct result of risk-averse sentiment amongst investors amid the current escalating geopolitical situation.

The stock market too traded lower in early trade but trimmed losses, with the Sensex trading 852.58 points higher to 74,098.61 at 2.30 p.m. The Nifty 50 was trading above 22,900. Analysts note that the Nifty must trade below 22,500 for bearishness to pertain.

articles.title: U.S. Fed holds interest rates steady despite surging inflation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The US Federal Reserve on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) held interest rates steady, in line with market expectations, days ahead of crucial midterm elections where surging inflation has been a key issue.

The 12-member Federal Open Market Committee voted 10-2 to hold rates at a target range between 3.75 and 4.00%, citing the need for more data in the fight against inflation, after having hiked for the first time in three years at its previous meeting in September.

“The accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the Committee’s two percent goal,” the Fed said in a statement announcing its decision.
Two members of the committee, Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, dissented, calling instead for an immediate 0.25-percentage-point rate hike.
The central bank has missed its long-term two-percent target for inflation for more than five years, with households and businesses battered by sustained price increases.

U.S. President Donald Trump's war on Iran, launched in late February, has sent energy prices skyrocketing and fueled domestic inflation, alongside his wide-ranging tariff policies. Prices have also been driven by an investment boom in artificial intelligence (AI) technology and the build-out of huge data centres to support it. The decision comes six days ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, in which the Democratic Party is seeking to wrest control of both houses of Congress from Mr. Trump's Republicans. Mr. Trump's handling of the economy has been a key issue throughout the campaign, with working-class households across the country struggling to make ends meet despite largely stable overall economic growth.
U.S. consumer inflation came in hotter than expected in September, clocking in at 3.7%, edging back towards a three-year high established in May.
Still, key policymakers at the Fed -- including Mr. Warsh -- have signalled that they did not see an urgency to raise rates again immediately.

Speaking in Bangkok earlier this month, Mr. Warsh said that U.S. economic conditions had “broadly conformed” to policymakers’ expectations, fueling speculation that the Fed may pause at the October meeting.
On Wednesday (October 28, 2026), the Fed said economic activity in the United States was expanding at a “strong” pace, upgrading its language from the FOMC meeting six weeks prior.

Wendy Edelberg, senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, told AFP before the meeting that a decision to hold after raising rates in September was potentially contradictory, given the labour market -- the Fed’s other mandate -- has been largely stable.
“In terms of the economics of it, I don’t totally understand the logic,” she said.

articles.title: G20 foreign ministers to end Atlanta meeting without consensus on key issues
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Top diplomats from the Group of 20 (G20) largest world economies will wrap up two days of talks in Atlanta on Saturday (October 31, 2026) without reaching consensus on several critical global security issues, after divisions, notably over Russia’s war with Ukraine, overshadowed the start of the meeting.

As a result, the group will not release a joint communique, but will rely on a chairman’s statement summarising the talks, which U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio will release at the conclusion, according to diplomats who attended.

Mr. Rubio, who opened the talks with an appeal for unity, cancelled the traditional group photograph of the foreign ministers on Friday (October 30, 2026), after European diplomats objected to the inclusion of Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and threatened to boycott or walk out of the photograph that often kicks off such gatherings.

Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski, who was representing his country for the first time as a guest at a G20 meeting, said on Friday he was not surprised by the failure to reach consensus. “We have wars going on, and we have participants in those wars around the table, so it’s very difficult to agree on a common line,” he told reporters.

Other participants, who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to discuss the closed-door talks, said all had agreed to try to overcome their differences despite the long odds, and to work to make next month’s G20 leaders’ summit, hosted by President Donald Trump in Florida, a success.

These diplomats said a chairman’s statement had long been the plan, given the deep differences among the attendees, including over the Russia-Ukraine conflict, the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran, U.S. tariffs and Chinese actions in the South China Sea.

All have contributed to spikes in the global cost of fuel, as well as uncertainty about trade. They described the opening session as cordial, but said Russia’s position on Ukraine is unyielding — as is its opposition to Poland’s membership in the G20. The disagreements also include the Trump administration’s decision not to invite G20 member South Africa, over the objections of others.

Some G20 countries had already expressed concern that the U.S. invited Russia during its heightened attacks on Ukraine, especially after Mr. Trump pushed ties with Ukraine to new lows by waiving fresh sanctions on Moscow and temporarily limiting logistical and intelligence assistance. However, the State Department announced on Friday that it had approved a proposed $2.1 billion sale of Patriot air defence interceptors for Ukraine.
Mr. Lavrov said Moscow would not allow a situation in which Ukraine poses a “military threat to legitimate security interests of the Russian Federation.”

He has travelled only infrequently to NATO member countries since Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022 and severe sanctions were imposed on Moscow, and it is unclear if Russian President Vladimir Putin will accept Mr. Trump’s invitation to attend the leaders’ summit at his Miami golf club in December 2026.

The U.S. has said a top priority for the meeting is resolving differences over issues related to freedom of navigation, particularly in the Strait of Hormuz, the Red Sea, the Black Sea and the South China Sea. The topic will include discussions on Iran, Russia-Ukraine and China and its smaller neighbours.

But hanging over the meeting is the prospect of new U.S. military intervention in Iran, which has put the region, including G20 member Saudi Arabia, on edge. Mr. Rubio met on the sidelines with his Saudi counterpart, Prince Faisal bin Farhan, as well as Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, whose country has been a key mediator.

articles.title: Trump backtracks on rallies in turbulent end to midterms campaign
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: U.S. President Donald Trump on Friday (October 30, 2026) insisted Republicans “have a shot” at success in the U.S. midterms, despite a feverish end to the campaign for elections that will decide control of Congress.
Mr. Trump reversed course and reinstated two rallies in Kansas and Iowa a day after cancelling them, a move that had raised questions about his health and about the state of the race.

“There’s such love in these all over the country,” he said of his rallies, before rattling off a series of insults against Democratic candidates vying for House and Senate seats in the elections on Tuesday (November 3, 2026).

Speaking late on Friday to a crowd in Daytona, Florida, Mr. Trump said the rallies were being held “for one very simple reason: to stop America-hating communists from taking over the United States Congress.”

He reiterated his promise to give every adult American citizen $5,000 if Republicans retain control of both chambers of Congress. Experts have questioned whether he has the legal authority to do that.

Earlier in the day, Mr. Trump acknowledged to reporters that a sitting President’s party often suffers in midterm elections. “I think we have a shot at doing well. Maybe very well, but you know, pretty well,” he said.

Mr. Trump, 80, said he had cancelled the two events to hold virtual rallies, but that Republicans in Iowa and Kansas called and “said if you could go, it would be better than a tele-rally.” His comments, however, were far from a robust assessment of Republican chances in Tuesday’s vote.

Republicans are defending their 53-47 majority in the Senate, while Democrats are seeking to capture at least one chamber of Congress and curb Mr. Trump’s legislative agenda during his final two years in office.

Mr. Trump has put himself at the centre of the Republicans’ midterm strategy, hoping it will fire up his MAGA (Make America Great Again) base. But his dismal approval ratings and public anger over the Iran war and the cost of living may be a drag on Republican chances.
Mr. Trump, who complained of losing his voice earlier this week, had lashed out on Thursday (October 29, 2026) when asked if he was scrapping the Kansas trip because he was “sick of traveling.”
“I feel perfect,” he snapped, saying he no longer needed to visit Kansas because Republican Senator Roger Marshall was “doing very well.”
But the about-face was likely the result of questions over the energy levels of America’s oldest-ever elected President, political strategist Mike Fahey told AFP .

fullParagraphs: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar met his Canadian counterpart Anita Anand and agreed that Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to Canada in December will be another “building block” in ties between the two countries.

Mr. Jaishankar met Ms. Anand in Atlanta on the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting on Friday (October 30, 2026). Both the leaders also assessed the “steady growth” in India-Canada cooperation.
“Delighted to meet FM @AnitaAnandMP of Canada today. Assessed the steady growth of our cooperation,” Jaishankar said in a post on X on Friday (October 30, 2026).

According to an official statement, “the ministers agreed that Prime Minister Modi’s visit to Canada in December will be another building block in the two countries’ ambitious relationship.” They also “agreed” to stay in close contact ahead of the visit, it said.

Earlier this month, during her visit to India, Canadian Foreign Minister Anand met Prime Minister Modi, and she said they had a productive discussion on further strengthening India-Canada ties in trade, technology and energy.
On October 16, the Indian High Commission in Ottawa said Mr. Modi will visit Canada on December 11 and 12. The date of the visit was also confirmed by Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney.
Mr. Carney had said he spoke to Modi and the visit will take place in Toronto and Ottawa. “We’ll see if we can broaden it out,” he said earlier this month.

articles.title: Oman rescues 25 from burning ship, Iran halts tankers
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Oman said Friday (October 30, 2026) it had rescued 25 sailors from a merchant ship set ablaze in an attack, as Iran reported three oil tankers were halted while crossing the Strait of Hormuz.
Tehran has restricted maritime traffic through the strait since the West Asia war erupted on February 28 with U.S.-Israeli strikes on the Islamic republic.
The narrow waterway, which normally carries about a fifth of global oil, has become a focal point of the conflict, with ships regularly coming under Iranian fire.

Muscat's navy "carried out an evacuation operation for 25 crew members of the merchant ship RITI, flying the Panamanian flag, after it was targeted, which led to a fire breaking out on board," Oman's Maritime Security Centre said in a statement.
The crew members were provided with medical care, the Omani statement said, without giving details.
The Marine Traffic ship-tracking website described the RITI as a crude oil tanker.

U.S. Central Command chief Brad Cooper said in a video released on Friday (October 30) that U.S. forces had "successfully cleared the strait's internationally recognised primary transit routes of Iranian sea mines".
U.S. forces remain "present to ensure that all primary transit routes in the Strait of Hormuz remain free and clear," he added.

Mr. Cooper said he visited some of the more than 50,000 U.S. service members in the region, repeating earlier statements that Washington has helped Gulf countries export more than 1.5 billion barrels of crude via the strait since summer.

British maritime security agency UKMTO said that a ship 40 nautical miles (74 kilometres) south of Lavan Island in Iran was struck on Friday (October 30) by an unknown projectile, which caused a fire onboard.
"The crew of the vessel have been reported as safe and there is no reported environmental impact at this time," the UKMTO said on X.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards said earlier that three oil tankers had been halted after encountering unspecified "incidents" or hitting mines.

articles.title: Fears of violence as France braces for Halloween protests
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: France on Saturday (October 31, 2026) braced for a third weekend of protests coinciding with Halloween, as shops boarded up and authorities scrambled to prevent a repeat of the street violence that swept the country two weeks ago.
The demonstrations come in an increasingly febrile political climate, with presidential elections six months away and far-right leader Marine Le Pen leading opinion polls.
President Emmanuel Macron this week said it was "not normal" for France to be in such a state of "turmoil" so close to a presidential election.
Around 70,000 security personnel will be deployed on Saturday (October 31, 2026), matching the number mobilised a week ago, as authorities seek to avert a repeat of the October 17 unrest.
More than 40 metro stations will be closed in the capital and tram services will also be disrupted.

An aide to Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said they expected street violence on a scale "comparable" to the unrest two weeks ago, when images of clashes, looted shops and public buildings set ablaze were broadcast around the world.

The protest movement brings together Yellow Vest activists, trade unions, and high school and university students. It initially focused on the rising cost of living, inequality, and deteriorating learning conditions.
But following a security clampdown and serious injuries to some protesters, the movement broadened its demands to include greater protection of civil liberties and the right to protest.
A police source pointed to "considerable nervousness" among the authorities. "There is no reason to think this will go smoothly," the source said.
Alain Di Crescenzo, president of France's chamber of commerce, said business owners were worried.

"Shopkeepers can't wait for Saturday (October 31, 2026) to be over," Mr. Di Crescenzo told broadcaster France Inter . "The information we have is that Halloween is not helping matters, because we're going to have people wearing masks."
Ahead of the protests, some shops and other businesses across France boarded up their storefronts.

articles.title: Flavio Bolsonaro says he left Brazil because he is the victim of 'persecution'
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Former conservative presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro said Friday (October 30, 2026) that he fled Brazil to the United States because he was a victim of "persecution" in his country.

Mr. Bolsonaro, who lost Sunday's (October 25) election runoff to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, secretly left Brazil on Tuesday (October 27) and arrived in Florida aboard a private jet on Wednesday (October 28) after travelling through Argentina and Ecuador.

"The persecution began even sooner than I imagined," the senator said during an Instagram livestream in which he discussed his decision to flee after his Brazilian passports were cancelled as part of a money laundering investigation.
In the video, he recounted how police informed him on Monday that his passports were being revoked as he left a visit to his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, who is under house arrest.
"With tears in his eyes, he told me: 'You know where they're going with this, don't you?'" he said of his father.
"I told him: 'Dad, I know... Now I know what I have to do,'" he recounted.
Although he gave no details of how he left the country, he said he and his wife made the decision "without anyone knowing" and urged people not to "point the finger at anyone."
U.S. President Donald Trump and Argentine President Javier Milei are under pressure to explain the involvement of the United States and Argentina in the senator's escape.
"I didn't leave Brazil; I left for Brazil," Flavio Bolsonaro said, alleging that Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes had made false accusations against him.
He also suggested there had been irregularities in the runoff, comparing them to "handball goals" that were not disallowed by VAR, without detailing what those irregularities might have been.
He also predicted that the economy would "go bust" under Lula and said he was willing to run for president again: "I'm not talking about 2030, I'm talking about before then."

articles.title: To overcome technical hurdles, ISRO flew NVS-03 satellite with pyro valves open: Narayanan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: ISRO chief V. Narayanan on Saturday (October 31, 2026) said that in order to ensure mission reliability and bypass previous technical hurdles, the NVS-03 satellite was operated with "three pyro valves open".

Addressing the media at a post-launch press conference, Mr. Narayanan revealed that this bold technical decision was validated after rigorous vibration and shock testing by a national-level committee chaired by former ISRO chief Kiran Kumar.
Pyro valves are crucial in spacecraft propulsion, and it may be recalled that the NVS-02 (launched in 2025), the second spacecraft in the NVS series, was a failure.
A high-level panel, after thorough analysis, concluded that "the drive signal did not reach the pyro valve of the oxidiser line of the engine meant for orbit raising."
In February 2026, ISRO, quoting the panel, announced that the most likely cause was the disengagement of at least one contact (in each of the main and redundant paths) of the connector.

Against this background, Mr. Narayanan said that with four satellites, including NVS-01 now active in India's navigation satellite system, ISRO plans to launch NVS-04 in five months, and NVS-05 in 10 months to further bolster the constellation.

Mr. Narayanan highlighted the exceptional accuracy of the flight. "Against [the planned] perigee [point when it is closest to the Earth] of 170.36 km; we have got 170.31 kilometres," Mr. Narayanan said.

"Against [the planned] Apogee [point farthest away from the Earth] of 37,247 kilometres, we achieved 38,080 kilometres," he noted. "This is one of the best accuracy of any of the launch vehicles in the world we can think of," he added.

The successful deployment has restored India's NavIC (Navigation with Indian Constellation) to its minimum operating configuration of four satellites, bolstering both strategic and civilian location services across the subcontinent.

Executing its fastest-ever turnaround for a heavy-lift rocket, the ISRO successfully placed the next-generation navigation satellite NVS-03 into a highly precise orbit using the GSLV-F18 launch vehicle early on Saturday (October 31).

He said: "To ensure mission reliability and bypass previous technical hurdles, ISRO flew the satellite with three pyro valves already open. Narayanan revealed that this bold technical decision was validated after rigorous vibration and shock testing by a national-level committee chaired by former ISRO chief Kiran Kumar."

Elaborating on NavIC's civilian applications, the ISRO chief said 10,400 locomotives and 64,000 fishing vessels are currently tracked in real-time. Under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana, the agency aims to expand this to 1 lakh fishing vessels within the next six months. In total, 15 lakh tracking devices have been fitted across vehicles. When asked when NavIC would be available on civilian mobile phones, Mr. Narayanan stated this would happen once the full seven-satellite constellation is completed.

articles.title: Meta settles, leaving Snap sole defendant in new social media trial
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Meta reached a settlement in a landmark case over the alleged harms of social media, the plaintiffs' lawyers said Friday, leaving Snap as the only defendant in a trial set to open in Los Angeles next week.

"We remain committed to improving safety for kids on social media apps and holding tech companies accountable, and we are pleased to have brought this matter to a just resolution on behalf of our client," Emily Jeffcott, a lawyer representing one of the young women suing both companies, said in a statement.
Jury selection began on Wednesday, and opening statements are scheduled for November 4.
The terms of the agreement are confidential, but sources close to Meta told AFP the company decided to settle for business reasons.

"Trials, dismissals and settlements are all common in the bellwether process, and this litigation is no exception," a Meta spokesperson said, referring to the series of test cases against the company being tried in Los Angeles.
If Snap does not settle, the trial will go ahead next week.
Snap did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
TikTok and YouTube were also named as defendants in the case, but both had already reached settlements with the plaintiffs, known by their initials SJ and KDB, their lawyers said.
A California state judge consolidated the two cases into a single trial.
Snap, which makes Snapchat, will defend itself against the claims of both SJ and KDB.

Lawyers for SJ and KDB will argue that their clients were exposed to "addictive and problematic" social media apps when they started using them at ages 13 and 15, respectively, according to court documents.

"We believe the evidence will support that we have put our community first, and that these allegations fundamentally misrepresent the plaintiffs' experiences on Snapchat and how our platform was designed," a Snap spokesperson said in a statement earlier this week.

articles.title: OpenAI to limit weapons information for teens on ChatGPT in violence-prevention push
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: OpenAI said on Friday it is tightening limits on the weapons-related information ChatGPT provides ​to teens, even when a question appears ‌harmless, as part of new safeguards aimed at ​preventing real-world violence.
The move comes ⁠as AI companies face growing scrutiny over the risks chatbots pose to young users and the companies’ ‌role in detecting threats of harm.
OpenAI will restrict practical ‌information on weapons and security systems that ‌could ⁠be misused , with the limits applying to ⁠teens even when there is no sign of violent intent
For all users, ChatGPT will be able to ​automatically end chats where ‌someone appears to be fixating on violence, and OpenAI may temporarily pause accounts after multiple such chats

The company also said ‌it strengthened its age prediction system to move ​users it estimates are under 18 into the teen experience, and it ⁠plans to notify parents if their teen’s account is paused for repeatedly discussing violence
For all ‌users, OpenAI is limiting detail on past mass attacks, including the weapons used and how they were obtained
The company said the new safeguards will begin rolling out in the next few weeks, and it will ‌continue to refine them
OpenAI said earlier this month ​that teens spend under 15 minutes a day on average on ChatGPT, in ⁠its first report on teen use

A report by ⁠non-profit Common Sense Media earlier this month found that ChatGPT’s teen version often ‌alerted parents late or not at all when teen accounts held conversations about suicide, self-harm ​or eating disorders

articles.title: A ferocious El Niño is brewing thanks to record Pacific heat
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: For most of this year, climate scientists have been closely monitoring the Niño 3.4 region in the central-equatorial Pacific — the primary index area to define the phases of the El Niño Southern Oscillation and the alarming amount of ocean heat closely tracking an El Niño. The world’s oceans beyond the poles reached a record-high average surface temperature of 21.18°C on August 22, and daily sea surface temperatures in the Niño 3.4 region have been consistently shattering records.

According to the U.S. NOAA’s Climate Prediction Center, a ‘strong to very strong’ El Niño is 83% likely, with a high chance of a historic event exceeding the strength of any previous El Niño since 1950.

The El Niño is a natural climate pattern that emerges every two to seven years and affects global weather and heightens the risk of extreme heatwaves and altered rainfall worldwide. But this year’s event has put the world more on edge.

articles.title: In Kashmir’s traditional rice, clues to a journey from East Asia
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: For many generations, Kashmir’s farmers have cultivated traditional varieties of rice — and a new study by researchers at the Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology (SKUAST-Kashmir), Srinagar, has found that these varieties carry a unique genetic history.

According to the study, published in The Plant Genome , Kashmir’s traditional varieties carry cold-tolerance and other locally adapted genes that modern varieties have partly lost, making them potentially valuable as climate change increases stress on crops.
The genetic analysis also indicated the varieties are more closely related to those from the Korean Peninsula and Northeast China.

articles.title: Beyond gullibility: On digital arrest scams
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant’s exasperation, during the Supreme Court’s hearing on October 29 on the “digital arrest” scams, that people still fall for such scams despite abundant warnings and orders from the Court is understandable. About ₹800 crore has been lost to these scams this year even after recoveries, a hefty sum from the savings of individual victims. But this is not merely about gullibility. Scammers posing as CBI or police officers succeed because their victims, older citizens in particular, defer to or fear law enforcement. When Indian police are widely seen as high-handed towards ordinary citizens and as serving only the powerful, the threat of an “arrest” over a video call cannot be that implausible for many. That said, the Court’s pressing of the Reserve Bank of India to finalise its KYC Amendment Directions, 2026, which require banks to flag suspected mule accounts and put temporary debit holds on them, is welcome. CBI investigations have shown that mule accounts are central to scammers laundering their proceeds after duping victims and that bank staff have, in some cases, helped open them. With the availability of complete transaction histories and AI tools, banks can now spot anomalous transactions faster. The Attorney-General’s assurance that the directions will be in force by December 31 is also welcome. The Court’s insistence that banks compensate victims addresses an issue with the RBI’s zero-liability provisions. Its 2017 circular covers only unauthorised transactions, leaving victims who were coerced into making transfers without any recourse.

Yet, full compensation for the victims whenever banks are found wanting in due diligence must be implemented with care as this might force banks to flag far more than the actual mule accounts. Already the RBI directions cast a wide net. Any transaction of ₹1,000 or more that is ‘unusual’ for an account holder’s declared profile, or linked to a reported account, can be held for up to 60 days, and longer if directed by the police. In cases where small traders and Jan Dhan account holders have unknowingly received transfers from mule accounts, freezing their accounts for two months or more is a disproportionate penalty. Also, the Court’s suggestion that unusual transactions must be automatically reported to the police and physically verified raises privacy concerns. These measures must ensure that genuine account holders are not penalised for bank failures. Many of these scams are run from compounds using trafficked Indians in conflict-ridden parts of Myanmar and in Cambodia and Laos where they have thrived due to some degree of official patronage. India must use its clout to pressure these regimes.

articles.title: Suboptimal outcomes: On social security boards for unorganised, gig, platform workers
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: One year after the implementation of the Code on Social Security , the Union Labour Ministry has constituted the National Social Security Boards for Unorganised Workers and Gig and Platform Workers. The constitution of the boards, though delayed, is a welcome step. However, the highly centralised nature of this mechanism may hinder its optimal outcomes. By design, the Union Government controls both the Boards: they will be chaired by Union Minister for Labour Mansukh Mandaviya. The Board for Unorganised Sector Workers will have 40 members, nominated by the Union Government. They include seven members representing unorganised sector workers and seven members representing employers of the unorganised sector. Similarly, the Board for the welfare of gig and platform workers will have 22 members with five representatives each from the aggregators and the workers. But they have no significant representation of Central Trade Unions from the Opposition side or from the State Governments ruled by the Opposition. Labour is in the Concurrent List of the Constitution and both the States and the Union must work together to improve the living standards of workers.

The International Labour Organization defines social security as the ‘protection that a society provides to individuals and households to ensure access to health care and to guarantee income security, particularly in cases of old age, unemployment, sickness, invalidity, work injury, maternity or loss of a breadwinner’. The Union Government claims that the country’s social security coverage has increased from 19% in 2015 to 64.3% in 2025, which is around 94 crore citizens. However, it is apparent that the unorganised and gig and platform workers, who make up more than 92% of the country’s total workforce, are far from enjoying any social security under this definition. Almost two decades ago, the National Commission for Enterprises in the Unorganised Sector, headed by economist Arjun Sengupta, recommended a slew of measures to improve the social security of workers in the informal sector. The issues raised by the panel still remain unaddressed. A report prepared by Justice V. Gopala Gowda for the Keralam Government in March this year flagged certain anti-federal and anti-worker characteristics in the Social Security Code and suggested amendments. The Union Government should take the trade unions and the State Governments on board while creating new systems and mechanisms to address the social security concerns of the vast majority of workers.

articles.title: Open to investigation: On the challenge to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The Digital News Publishers Association’s (DNPA) challenge to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 , and its Rules , has drawn attention to concerns that a law to safeguard informational privacy risks creating a serious chilling effect on the media. The absence of a specific exemption for journalistic activity could subject reporters investigating official misconduct or corruption to the obligations of a “data fiduciary”, requiring them to notify and seek consent from the very individuals they are investigating. Such onerous requirements could affect investigations undertaken in the public interest. The implications extend to routine newsgathering too, where personal information is integral to reporting. The omission is particularly consequential because the drafts in 2018, 2019 and 2021 carried a journalistic exemption. The Act already provides exemptions for certain forms of data processing, including for research and statistical purposes, making the denial of similar protection to journalists difficult to justify. Non-compliance can attract penalties of up to ₹250 crore, posing an existential threat to smaller and independent newsrooms. The DNPA petition also challenges Section 44(3), which amended the RTI Act, 2005, removing the earlier public-interest qualification concerning disclosure of personal information. The protection of personal information must not be absolute; an overriding public interest must remain a legitimate ground for disclosure, particularly when the information is held by public authorities. Investigations into corruption often rely on asset disclosures and tender documents containing personal data. Restricting access to these records risks reducing journalism to merely reproducing government releases.

The Supreme Court, while issuing notice on the petition, rightly emphasised the need to balance press freedom with the right to privacy. Although journalists in India enjoy no specific statutory protection for their work, freedom of the press is constitutionally protected under Article 19(1)(a). The Court has also shielded newspapers from arbitrary state restrictions. However, growing mistrust of legacy media and the rise of independent content creators have made it difficult to determine who receives such protection. The Centre has also flagged this concern. Yet, carving out distinct categories is no easy task — a 2026 Reuters Institute report shows that the proportion of 18- to 24-year-olds identifying social media as their primary source of news rose from 21% in 2015 to 39% in 2025. A purely legalistic determination of these competing concerns may perhaps prove too onerous. Stakeholders must build consensus on a mutually acceptable framework where public functionaries and those handling public funds are not insulated from scrutiny under the guise of privacy. Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw’s indication that he would meet editors is a welcome step towards consensus.

articles.title: Deemed ineligible: On the Supreme Court and SIR
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: At Wednesday’s hearing of a petition on the Delhi SIR in the Supreme Court, Justice Joymalya Bagchi asked questions that cut to the heart of the Election Commission of India (ECI)’s SIR of electoral rolls . If an existing voter was “lax, inert or did not respond” to enumeration forms, was that a ground for the ECI to “forfeit his or her right to vote forever”? The Bench headed by the Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said that the ECI was in “error” to force such voters, struck off for not returning enumeration forms, to reapply on Form 6 as if they were new voters. It asked why voters who had shifted residences could not just disclose details and why deleted voters could not fill enumeration forms belatedly. This is the central design flaw of the SIR as it shifts the burden of enrolment from the state to the elector, including those who have voted before, and treats a mere change of address as ground for deletion. The share of draft deletions recorded as “shifted” or “absent” rose from 55% in Bihar to 72% in States/Union Territories in Phase 3. In Karnataka, about 84 lakh electors were deleted, marked as “shifted” or “absent” during enumeration. But only a net of 8.2 lakh, including new electors, were added during the claims phase, with the final roll being 64.5 lakh short of the projected adult population. Requiring moved voters to re-register as fresh applicants defeats the ECI’s historic mandate of widening the franchise, which was inherent in the 2002-03 intensive revision, where enumerators enrolled shifted voters at their new homes and the Chief Electoral Officer reconciled the old entries.

Justice Bagchi also mentioned that the Bihar judgment was not a “binding precedent” and that the legality of “logical discrepancy” checks, allowed only as an “interim arrangement” in West Bengal, had not been finally adjudicated. No statute or rule provides for judging a voter’s eligibility on the basis of family size or the age gap between voters and parents, which were two of the ECI’s ludicrous and algorithm-driven “logical discrepancy” checks. In West Bengal these checks resulted in massive disenfranchisement and The Hindu’s analysis found that in Delhi, Muslims were disproportionately flagged. But the Court should not merely issue managerial fixes such as extended deadlines or displaying printed lists in blocks, as it has in the past. The final SIR rolls are erroneous as deletions flowed from a flawed design rather than just lapses by the ECI. The dead and duplicate entries that the SIR identified should be removed and newly eligible electors added. Voters wrongly removed from draft rolls must be included again. The larger questions over the Commission’s SIR conduct and how its members are appointed must also be settled.

articles.title: Clinging on: On Netanyahu and the Israel elections
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Benjamin Netanyahu was at the centre of Israel’s October 27 elections. For Israel’s longest-serving Prime Minister, who oversaw a genocidal war in Gaza following Hamas’s October 7 attack , the election was the biggest test of his political career. For the Opposition, which promised to hold him accountable for the failures of October 7 and end the country’s “forever wars”, the election offered an opportunity to oust him from power. The results, however, sent a mixed message. With 85.6% of the votes counted, Mr. Netanyahu’s right-religious coalition has lost its majority but is still the largest bloc . His Likud party is projected to win 26 seats, while its main rival Yashar, led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, is expected to secure 21. Otzma Yehudit and Religious Zionism, the far-right extremist parties in Mr. Netanyahu’s coalition, demonstrated their continued strength, winning 13 seats between them. The dark horse, however, could be the Arab parties — the Joint List is projected to win 12 seats while the United Arab List (Ra’am) could secure seven seats. With neither bloc commanding a majority, the Arab parties could propel the opposition coalition to power. But the big question is whether the anti-Netanyahu coalition is ready to join hands with the Arab parties, which have historically been kept on the margins of Israel’ s power politics.

Mr. Netanyahu’s central promise has been that only he can guarantee Israel’s security. Yet, the October 7 attack took place on his watch and he has refused to take responsibility for the failures that led to it. A wanted man by the International Criminal Court, he has repeated, before and after October 7, that a Palestine state would not be formed while he is in power. His war on Gaza has killed over 70,000 Palestinians, including 20,000 children, and displaced the region’s population. Israel’s brutal occupation machinery has also expanded and tightened its control of the West Bank, while settler terrorists have unleashed violence on Palestinian households. His war on Iran has been a disaster, with global economic consequences. Mr. Netanyahu has sought to portray his wars as bold, necessary moves to protect Israel, while exploiting Israelis’ security concerns for political gain. He may not be voted out immediately, but his failure to secure a majority and the decline in his party’s popularity are significant. The Opposition should take its cue from the results and form a broad coalition with the Arab parties. It should restore accountability in governance, revisit his unchecked militarism and rebuild ties with the world. If Mr. Netanyahu continues to cling to power, it would be bad news for Israel and the region.

articles.title: Hunker down: On Cyclone Arnab, its landfall
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Cyclone Arnab, the first named storm of the North Indian Ocean cyclone season this year, intensified rapidly before making landfall as a ‘very severe cyclonic storm’ on October 28. This particular rapidity is a challenge for forecasters and some models did fail to anticipate how strong Arnab would become. It also moved faster than expected towards the coast, before stalling for a time and beginning the landfall process several hours before the India Meteorological Department (IMD) had predicted it would, in the middle of the night, leaving many district authorities with a potentially narrower window to evacuate high-risk settlements. With core wind speeds of 125-135 kilometres per hour, it delivered more than 100 mm of rain over parts of Anakapalli, Visakhapatnam, Kalingapatnam, Kakinada and Machilipatnam, in Andhra Pradesh. But even though it has completed landfall, southern Odisha likely faces a greater threat only hence. Early reports claimed no loss of life in Andhra Pradesh or Odisha, which has been attributed to the disaster management operations in both States; the Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister, N. Chandrababu Naidu, said there were five deaths in Andhra Pradesh . Regrettably, the suspension of transport services, including road connectivity and flights, closure of schools and offices, and power cuts to minimise risks posed by loose wires remains an essential part of saving lives, entailing other social and economic disruptions that the States must account for, and address, in their post-storm assessments.

Odisha may have to brace for rainfall and waters due to moisture in the storm’s outer circulation, which will arrive over land that has recovered in patches from the fourth wettest monsoon in the State’s history. Extreme rainfall after repeated flooding may face soil that has not drained fully, raising the risk of more flooding following even lower levels of rainfall, and slope failures in hilly terrain. Farmers in Ganjam and Puri have already voiced worries about the risk of prolonged inundation destroying paddy crops, compounding the already considerable financial consequences of the southwest monsoon; Ganjam alone had lost 33% of crops by October. In Sundargarh, however, farmers hope that Arnab will relieve moisture stress in standing crops after a dry month. The IMD has already issued alerts in the Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri, Nabarangpur, and Kalahandi districts, before the rainbelt extends further north. The relatively low figure of deaths will be a testament to proactive governance. However, it is past time that States adopted a zero-disruption approach, especially since property and infrastructure were damaged, and the risk of people being pushed into poverty over lost possessions and livelihoods persists.

Early reports claimed no loss of life in Andhra Pradesh or Odisha, which has been attributed to the disaster management operations in both States; the Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister, N. Chandrababu Naidu, said there were five deaths in Andhra Pradesh . Regrettably, the suspension of transport services, including road connectivity and flights, closure of schools and offices, and power cuts to minimise risks posed by loose wires remains an essential part of saving lives, entailing other social and economic disruptions that the States must account for, and address, in their post-storm assessments.
articles.keyPoints:
• Cyclone Arnab, the first named storm of the North Indian Ocean cyclone season this year, intensified rapidly before making landfall as a ‘very severe cyclonic storm’ on October 28. This particular rapidity is a challenge for forecasters and some models did fail to anticipate how strong Arnab would become. It also moved faster than expected towards the coast, before stalling for a time and beginning the landfall process several hours before the India Meteorological Department (IMD) had predicted it would, in the middle of the night, leaving many district authorities with a potentially narrower window to evacuate high-risk settlements. With core wind speeds of 125-135 kilometres per hour, it delivered more than 100 mm of rain over parts of Anakapalli, Visakhapatnam, Kalingapatnam, Kakinada and Machilipatnam, in Andhra Pradesh. But even though it has completed landfall, southern Odisha likely faces a greater threat only hence. Early reports claimed no loss of life in Andhra Pradesh or Odisha, which has been attributed to the disaster management operations in both States; the Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister, N. Chandrababu Naidu, said there were five deaths in Andhra Pradesh . Regrettably, the suspension of transport services, including road connectivity and flights, closure of schools and offices, and power cuts to minimise risks posed by loose wires remains an essential part of saving lives, entailing other social and economic disruptions that the States must account for, and address, in their post-storm assessments.
• Odisha may have to brace for rainfall and waters due to moisture in the storm’s outer circulation, which will arrive over land that has recovered in patches from the fourth wettest monsoon in the State’s history. Extreme rainfall after repeated flooding may face soil that has not drained fully, raising the risk of more flooding following even lower levels of rainfall, and slope failures in hilly terrain. Farmers in Ganjam and Puri have already voiced worries about the risk of prolonged inundation destroying paddy crops, compounding the already considerable financial consequences of the southwest monsoon; Ganjam alone had lost 33% of crops by October. In Sundargarh, however, farmers hope that Arnab will relieve moisture stress in standing crops after a dry month. The IMD has already issued alerts in the Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri, Nabarangpur, and Kalahandi districts, before the rainbelt extends further north. The relatively low figure of deaths will be a testament to proactive governance. However, it is past time that States adopted a zero-disruption approach, especially since property and infrastructure were damaged, and the risk of people being pushed into poverty over lost possessions and livelihoods persists.

articles.title: Traffic curbs in Delhi for INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan on November 1 | LIVE
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP) on Saturday (October 31) questioned the timing of the INDIA bloc’s November 1 rally being held amid Diwali festivities and said that ignoring festivals, social harmony and the country’s economy in the name of politics is not a good sign for political parties.

The RSS affiliate pointed out that Congress leader Rahul Gandhi’s Bharat Jodo Yatra, held between September 2022 and January 2023, had a nine-day break from December 25 to January 2 for Christmas and New Year celebrations.

However, despite repeated appeals by traders’ organisations in Delhi and members of Hindu society to cancel or postpone the November 1 rally, their pleas have fallen on deaf ears, VHP national spokesperson Vinod Bansal said in a post on X.
Traffic restrictions will be in place across parts of Delhi from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. on November 1 in view of an INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan, police said.

Traffic diversions will be enforced at key intersections in central Delhi, including Netaji Subhash Marg T-point, Rajghat, Delhi Gate, ITO A-point, Ajmeri Gate red light, Ranjeet Singh Flyover, Jhandewalan roundabout, Turkman Gate and Mirdard Chowk, depending on the traffic situation, the Delhi Traffic Police said.

Commuters are likely to face congestion on Bahadur Shah Zafar Marg between ITO and Delhi Gate, Jawaharlal Nehru Marg between Rajghat and Ajmeri Gate, Aruna Asaf Ali Road, Minto Road, Desh Bandhu Gupta Road and Barakhamba Road, as well as stretches around Kamla Market and Hamdard Chowk.
Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge has refused to comment on whether CJP leaders will participate in the November 1 rally in Delhi planned by the opposition against SIR .
PTI had on Thursday (October 28) erroneously reported that Mr. Kharge had replied in the negative taking note of his gesture. However, his office clarified he did not wish to comment on the question.

The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has extended support to the November 1 rally. The outfit, founded by Abhijeet Dipke, said it would support organisations fighting for free and fair elections and reiterated its demand for Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation.

Ahead of the INDIA bloc’s November 1 rally at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan against “vote chori”, the Haryana Congress on Friday held meetings in Karnal, Panipat and Sonipat for finalising a strategy to ensure maximum participation at the event from the state, party leaders said.
The Congress in-charge for Haryana, Sanjay Dutt, and State unit president, Rao Narendra Singh, took part in the meetings with senior party leaders, district office-bearers and workers.

The meetings reviewed the preparations for the ‘Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao’ rally in Delhi, which will be led by Congress leader Rahul Gandhi at the Ramlila Maidan as part of the opposition bloc’s campaign against alleged electoral irregularities and the demand for the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

articles.title: KTR questions proposed sale of IDBI Bank, asks if its valuable real estate assets were factored in valuation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) working president K.T. Rama Rao has questioned the Union government’s proposed sale of IDBI Bank to a private player , raising concerns over the bank’s valuation, changes in bidding norms and the treatment of its real estate assets.

In a post on X, KTR said public sector undertakings (PSUs) and public sector banks were national assets that needed to be safeguarded. He said reports about the alleged undervaluation of IDBI Bank were a matter of concern and sought to know why the rules and valuation methodology were changed after bids fell below the reserve price.
He also questioned whether the bank’s valuable real estate assets, including prime land in Hyderabad, were adequately factored into the valuation.
KTR sought to know why the concerns raised by IDBI Bank employees over the proposed disinvestment were not being addressed.

Before selling a reputed public sector bank to a private entity, the Union government owed the country clear answers on the valuation and the process being followed, he said. Questioning the urgency behind the proposed sale, the BRS leader asked: “What’s the hurry?”.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Congress, VCK mobilise cadres for Nov. 1 INDIA bloc protest in New Delhi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, the Tamil Nadu Congress Committee (TNCC) and Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi (VCK) have activated their respective party machineries to mobilise cadres for the INDIA bloc protest to be held on November 1, 2026, in New Delhi.

While the bulk of the heavy lifting would be done by the Indian National Congress, which is much stronger in and around New Delhi, the TNCC leaders, on their part, are expected to mobilise at least 150 people from every district in Tamil Nadu.
Mayiladuthurai MP R. Sudha said that the party’s rank and file are enthusiastic and have heeded the call of Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, who is expected to lead the protest.

“We expect more than five lakh Congress cadres to participate. From Tamil Nadu, we are expecting at least 100 party workers to reach New Delhi from each district. Apart from them, the office-bearers of the Mahila Congress, Youth Congress, and other party wings will also participate,” she said.

While the Congress party is mobilising people from across the country, Ms. Sudha alleged that the BJP-led Centre was trying to curtail the privileges of Members of Parliament by not allowing Emergency Quotas in trains and not providing accommodation to their guests.

“EQ is not being released. Family members are not being given accommodation, which we are usually allotted. Congress MPs, in particular, are being singled out. They are curtailing our privileges and our movement. This is an undeclared emergency,” she said.

A senior VCK leader said that the party has asked its organs in Tamil Nadu and across southern States such as Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, and Keralam to mobilise a modest number of party cadres for the protest in New Delhi.

articles.title: Operation underway to recover bodies from remote chopper crash site in Uttarakhand
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Operations to recover the bodies of the six victims of the helicopter crash in Uttarakhand resumed on Saturday (October 31, 2026) morning, officials said.

Rescue work started at 5 a.m. on Saturday (October 31, 2026) but the recovery from the remote area would be difficult, they said. The operation had been halted on Friday (October 30, 2026) due to darkness, the presence of wild bears and other animals and difficult terrain.

A privately run helicopter carrying pilgrims from Badrinath crashed into a hillside in Joshimath in Uttarakhand, killing all six of its occupants. The helicopter, operated by Trans Bharat Aviation, was returning from the Badrinath shrine to Dehradun.
The bodies of the pilot and the five pilgrims from Karnataka were found in the vicinity of the wreckage in Chai village.
The district administration said that on Saturday (October 31, 2026) morning a team from the forest department was also dispatched to the site to recover the bodies.
A team from the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB), which is probing the crash, will also be reaching the site on the day.
Speaking to reporters, Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami said that orders have been issued to investigate and determine the exact cause of the accident.

"We pray to God to grant the departed souls a place at his divine feet and give strength to their families and loved ones, who are going through immense grief and trauma during this difficult time," Mr. Dhami said.

Prateek Jain, CEO, Uttarakhand Civil Aviation Development Authority (UCADA) told PTI , "The bodies were found but the recovery is difficult due to the terrain. The mortal remains will be brought to Chamoli district headquarters via a trek and after post-mortem examination, it will be brought to Dehradun."
When asked about permission for flying despite an alert issued by IMD, Mr. Jain said, "We had also issued an advisory but that is in the scope of investigation now."
On Friday (October 30, 2026), officials had informed that after recovery, the bodies will be brought to Joshimath town where post-mortem will be conducted on Saturday (October 31, 2026).
The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has also said that its team has been dispatched to Dehradun to conduct a preliminary and regulatory assessment of the accident.
